audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph second ark procession, Levitical organization, music, sacrifices, and Michal, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed against 2 Samuel 6 for David's houses and tent, exclusive Levite transport, assignment counts, blame for first breach, sanctification, skilled music, gatekeepers, animal offerings, royal clothing, public procession, and Michal's omitted speech.

verses.restored: David made houses for himself in city of David, prepared a place for ark of Divine, and pitched a tent for it.
Then David said, None should carry ark of Divine except Levites, for YHWH chose them to carry ark and minister before YHWH continually.
David gathered all Israel to Jerusalem to bring ark of YHWH to place he prepared.
David assembled descendants of Aaron and Levites:
from sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief and one hundred twenty relatives;
from sons of Merari, Asaiah the chief and two hundred twenty relatives;
from sons of Gershom, Joel the chief and one hundred thirty relatives;
from sons of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief and two hundred relatives;
from sons of Hebron, Eliel the chief and eighty relatives;
from sons of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief and one hundred twelve relatives.
David called Zadok and Abiathar the priests and Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.
He said, You are heads of Levite ancestral houses. Sanctify yourselves, you and relatives, and bring ark of YHWH Divine of Israel to place I prepared.
Because you were not there/ did not carry it at first, YHWH our Divine broke out against us, because we did not seek according to proper order.
Priests and Levites sanctified themselves to bring ark of YHWH Divine of Israel.
Levites carried ark of Divine on shoulders with poles, as Moses commanded according to word of YHWH.
David told Levite chiefs to appoint relatives as singers with instruments—harps, lyres, and cymbals—raising sounds of joy.
Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; Asaph son of Berechiah; and from Merari relatives, Ethan son of Kushaiah.
With them relatives of second rank: Zechariah, Ben/Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, gatekeepers.
Singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan sounded bronze cymbals.
Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah played lyres according to Alamoth.
Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah played harps according to Sheminith, to lead.
Chenaniah chief of Levites was over carrying/song; he instructed because he was skilled.
Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for ark.
Shebaniah, Jehoshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer the priests sounded trumpets before ark; Obed-edom and Jehiah were gatekeepers.
David, elders of Israel, and commanders of thousands went to bring ark of covenant of YHWH from house of Obed-edom with joy.
When Divine helped Levites carrying ark of covenant of YHWH, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
David was clothed in robe of fine linen, as were all Levites carrying ark, singers, and Chenaniah leader of carrying/song; David wore linen ephod.
All Israel brought ark of covenant of YHWH with shouting, horn, trumpets, cymbals, lyres, and harps.
As ark of covenant of YHWH came to city of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked through window and saw king David dancing and playing, and despised him in her heart.

translation_notes: The second attempt improves role clarity and transport method, but safer procedure does not explain away Uzzah's death or make it deserved.
David says Levites caused the first breach by not participating properly, yet he led the original plan. Responsibility may not be shifted downward onto workers after a leadership failure.
Ritual sanctification and 'proper order' must not become victim-blaming, purity policing, or fear that minor procedural mistakes merit death.
The chapter preserves extensive skilled musical and logistical labor. Chenaniah leads because of competence, not merely ancestry.
Gatekeepers, carriers, instrumentalists, singers, priests, and organizers all share responsibility; religious work is collaborative and should be safe and compensated.
Fourteen animals are killed in celebration. Their deaths should not disappear beneath music and pageantry.
Fine clothing and royal performance may communicate solidarity, but public spectacle does not remove hierarchy.

Chronicles gives Michal only an interior judgment and omits her confrontation, David's retaliatory speech, servant-women context, and childlessness from 2 Samuel 6. Her perspective must not be reduced to jealous contempt.
Alamoth and Sheminith are technical musical terms of uncertain meaning and require audit.
safety_note: Do not blame Uzzah or lower-ranking workers for leadership failure, weaponize ritual purity, exploit musicians, or use Michal as a misogynistic warning against women who criticize male religious spectacle. Safety, skill, shared responsibility, and dissent belong inside worship.
